primary_issue: Core Bayesian workflow is broadly sound, but fixed d_loo evidence bands and advice to switch from problematic LOO to WAIC are not generally valid; WAIC is not a remedy for influential observations. Pickle loading is unsafe for untrusted artifacts.

Strong scope and censoring guidance, but the CIF example destructures the function as three return values although the API returns time plus a cumulative-incidence array. Treating competing events as censored is valid for cause-specific hazards but must not be interpreted as CIF/subdistribution risk. Claims that Uno C is required for any cross-dataset comparison are overbroad.

Contains material statistical errors: p-values are reduced to P(data|H0), Bayesian methods are said to work with any sample size, and failed normality tests automatically route to rank tests even though these answer different estimands and normality tests are sample-size sensitive. Fixed Durbin-Watson/VIF/event-per-variable rules and blanket Likert/observational claims are not defensible as universal rules.

Useful code patterns, but diagnostic p-value dichotomies and automatic robust-SE fallback oversimplify model misspecification; AIC/BIC and likelihood-ratio comparison require comparable likelihood/data and nested-model conditions not fully stated.

Overclaims generalization without tuning across bacteria/organoids/stains and says manual parameter tuning is eliminated (11,17).; Parameter table says increasing cellprob_threshold finds more cells (268), while actual examples/troubleshooting use a lower value (-2) for more detections (369); the guidance is internally contradictory.; API/model examples are tied to older Cellpose model names and return shapes without a tested version pin (54-55,100-116,264-273).; No ground-truth sampling, boundary/object metrics, failure-stratum QC or uncertainty gate before morphometry.

Recipe recommends dividing fluorescence by PnR for cross-sample comparison (305-321); detector range is not a biological normalization and ignores compensation, transforms, acquisition settings, controls and batch effects.; Best practice says preserve flow.text on re-export (272), which can propagate instrument/sample identifiers and stale acquisition metadata into modified data.; Troubleshooting suggests bypassing offset validation (328-330) without a provenance/corruption warning.; FlowIO is correctly scoped as parser, but downstream ML suggestions need compensation, QC, gating and transformation controls.

Plugin installs are unpinned and community plugins have separate trust/supply-chain risk (31-42,373-381).; Screenshots and threshold overlays are illustrative; they must not replace blinded/quantitative segmentation validation.; Axis and scale metadata must be explicitly verified for real microscopy files.

16-bit scientific images are globally min-max normalized to 8-bit before thresholding (139-144,395-396), making thresholds incomparable across images and discarding intensity calibration.; The 'rolling ball' recipe is a Gaussian blur subtraction, not a rolling-ball algorithm (372-388).; MOG2 moving-contour counts are presented as cell counts without camera/stage drift, photobleaching, focus, object identity or temporal validation (216-251).; Reported contour count includes contours later skipped by area filter in annotation output (357-369).

Default initialization downloads a large external runtime on first use (49), so execution requires explicit supply-chain/network approval.; Inline macros and plugin commands depend on global ImageJ state, update sites and command parameter names; static review cannot establish correctness (137-160,213-318).; Axis round trips must be checked against actual TZCYX metadata; a copied array shape is not sufficient proof.; Headless TrackMate recipe is complex and unverified against a pinned TrackMate version (500-568).

Hard-coded CZYX/ZCYX/HWC assumptions (85-94,237-239) require metadata-aware axis validation.; Generic Otsu/watershed/object-size thresholds are illustrative and should be tuned on representative, blinded ground truth (142-174,306-337,394-398).; Co-positive pixels are not equivalent to cell-level co-localization; threshold choice, bleed-through and controls matter (233-239,425-440).

Claims tp.motion.characterize returns alpha/D_app (232-266), an API not established by the cited Trackpy surface and likely hallucinated/version-specific.; Says linking is a Hungarian bipartite assignment (128-130), an oversimplification of Trackpy subnet/linking behavior.; Best practice says always compute/subtract drift (441), but estimating drift from mobile particles can erase real collective motion; troubleshooting later admits immobile references are required (567), an internal contradiction.; Diffusion fit uses the first ten points with a free intercept and no localization-error, motion-blur, track-length weighting or uncertainty model (205-229).; 3D stack reshape assumes acquisition ordering and dimensions without metadata verification (360-364).

Plotting coverage is useful, but the statistical-comparison workflow fabricates a fixed ** annotation without running any test. That is unsafe scientific code generation and disqualifies the entry as-is.

The output is described as self-contained but requires an unpinned live CDN. User-controlled title/subtitle are inserted into HTML without escaping, enabling local HTML/script injection; only structure data is JSON-escaped. Normal-mode visualization is qualitative and lacks unit/provenance checks.

Generally useful layout guidance, but the proprietary declaration alone blocks content adoption. It also calls a PDF containing raster-composited panels a vector output, which can mislead users about editability/resolution.

License blocks adoption. The box-plot recipe silently chooses Mann-Whitney for any two groups, computes statistics inside plotting, reports only stars, and ignores pairing/design/estimand; PCA is applied without scaling or missingness/design checks. KM omits risk tables, censoring validation, and inferential context.

Broad and mostly plausible plotting reference. Simulated volcano/dose-response examples should not be mistaken for inferential workflows, and HTML export needs explicit self-contained/CDN/privacy policy. No critical statistical engine is embedded.

The strongest visualization guide in scope: it emphasizes exact p-values, effects, sample size and CVD-safe palettes. Journal requirements remain mutable and must be checked against the target journal rather than treated as evergreen.

Contains a concrete scientific labeling error: seaborn clustermap standard_scale=0 performs min-max scaling, not z-scoring, yet the comments/colorbar say z-score. Volcano example names a raw p-value threshold padj_thresh, and a simulated RNA/protein correlation plot actually generates independent RNA terms for x and y.

The guide encourages stars and qualitative labels instead of exact adjusted p-values/effect estimates. Its ANOVA example follows an omnibus parametric test with pairwise Mann-Whitney tests without design justification. Helper dh/barh are documented as axes fractions but added directly to data-coordinate y, so placement is dimensionally wrong.

The workflow hard-codes GRCh38 download/build examples and an unverified 2x/identical-results claim; read group, alt-contig, duplicate, contamination, and reference-bundle choices remain analysis-specific.
Recipes expose low-level indexed I/O but do not establish coordinate/build invariants or safe write semantics; pileup/filter behavior is parameter- and htslib-version-dependent.
Command recipes can silently discard records through flag/MAPQ filters or change representation through CRAM conversion; reference identity and provenance must be pinned.

Pins STAR/GENCODE examples to a moving release and treats generic two-pass settings as broadly suitable; read length, overhang, multimapping, chimeric reads, and annotation/reference coupling require assay-specific validation.

Annotation quality depends on the separately downloaded Bakta database release and taxonomic scope; predicted function is not experimentally validated and the prose license is conflated with tool/data licenses.
A legacy database/tool chain is presented as a general bacteria/archaea/virus solution; fragmented assemblies and stale reference databases can propagate false or generic product names.

Roary clustering is sensitive to annotation consistency, fragmentation, paralogs, identity threshold, and population structure; presence/absence association is not causal and default intermediate cleanup is mutating.
Tree importance from co-expression is association, not directed or causal regulation; stochasticity, TF-list coverage, cell-state confounding, and missing motif validation are not resolved.
A broad cookbook mixes local algorithms with remote Entrez/BLAST and external aligners; sequence submission can disclose unpublished data and examples are not version-pinned.
Remote Entrez/BLAST plus external MUSCLE/Clustal wrappers introduce network, privacy, executable, and version drift; phylogeny recipes do not establish model adequacy or uncertainty.
Hard-coded undocumented-looking /api/v1 response schemas and printed numerical outputs are not backed by a snapshot or retrieval evidence; ARCHS4 content and processing versions are mutable.

A wrapper over many independently changing services includes legacy PICR/old method signatures; cross-database mappings are many-to-many and release-dependent, yet no executable compatibility matrix is proved.
Study/profile identifiers and clinical endpoints are mutable; recipes risk denominator/sample-vs-patient errors and unadjusted survival/treatment inference from observational cancer cohorts.

Genotype-to-prescribing text is clinically actionable but omits diplotype calling, allele-function uncertainty, guideline version/effective date, ancestry, contraindications, and clinician/pharmacist review gates.

Clinical significance is condition-, inheritance-, submitter-, review-date-, transcript-, and assembly-specific; string matching Pathogenic is not a clinical interpretation workflow and conflicting/withdrawn assertions can be mishandled.

The skill assumes a JSON REST surface at cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cosmic/api and constructs Basic auth from plaintext email/password without locally frozen API documentation; commercial-use terms and credential exposure make it unsuitable.
rsIDs can be merged or withdrawn and frequencies are study/population/build-specific; a dbSNP record or ClinVar link does not establish pathogenicity.
Chronos gene effect and per-gene correlations are release-, cell-line-, copy-number-, lineage-, and missingness-dependent; correlation does not establish target dependency or therapeutic index.
Declared license is Unknown and accessions/files/checksums/assemblies are mutable; bulk URLs and sample metadata require provenance capture and human-subject/privacy screening.

Assay, biosample, replicate, audit, preferred-file, assembly, and pipeline-version filters determine validity; broad search recipes can mix incomparable experiments and SCREEN response schemas are not frozen.
Unpinned Ensembl REST defaults make IDs, coordinates, transcripts, sequences, and VEP consequences change across releases; assembly and canonical-transcript assumptions must be explicit.
NCBI Gene symbols/aliases and cross-species records are not one-to-one; E-utilities results are mutable and summaries are descriptive evidence, not functional or clinical truth.

GEO matrices are heterogeneous in normalization/platform and sample labels; generic extraction cannot support DE without study-specific design/QC, and patient metadata may be sensitive despite public hosting.

One skill spans many mutable services and optional local executables; ancillary text internally labels AlphaFold access as a local ColabFold/OpenMM model and includes COSMIC passwords, so version/API/provenance boundaries are not trustworthy.
The quick start labels BRCA1 pLI about 5.5e-38 as very high LoF intolerance even though pLI ranges 0-1 and that value is near zero; population frequency/constraint is not pathogenicity evidence.

Catalog associations are ancestry-, LD-, phenotype-, build-, and publication-dependent and are not causal; PRS construction needs harmonization, effect alleles, ancestry calibration, and external validation absent here.

The code treats JASPAR PFM as position-keyed although API PFMs are base-keyed arrays, computes maximum score by summing all positive bases rather than per-position maxima, and scans only the forward strand.

KEGG permits academic REST use but non-academic redistribution/use may require a commercial license; records are mutable and pathway membership does not establish mechanism or enrichment significance.
Aggregated disease-gene-phenotype edges differ in evidence type and model organism; phenotype matching is prioritization, not diagnosis, and API/ontology versions are not pinned.
Project-scoped measures require sex, age, diet, strain, batch, and study-design context; cross-project means and ontology matches are not directly comparable or causal.
GO annotations must retain evidence code, qualifier, taxon, date, and ontology release; electronic and experimental annotations cannot be pooled as equivalent biological proof.
A mutable web endpoint and assumed JSON schema are used as an API; scores/ranks are functional-prioritization evidence, not pathogenicity, causality, or tissue-matched validation.
A static 2022 ChIP-seq atlas is queried through an assumed API schema; assembly, antibody, cell context, peak quality, blacklist, and experiment redundancy determine whether overlap is meaningful.
UCSC coordinates are 0-based half-open while many genomic conventions differ; assembly/track version and table schema are mutable, making silent off-by-one or build mismatch likely.
Tree rendering/manipulation is useful but NCBI taxonomy is network/version dependent and topology alone lacks model support, rooting, branch uncertainty, and orthology validation.
Motif enrichment is dominated by background construction, GC/length bias, peak quality, motif redundancy, and genome build; motif presence is not TF binding or regulation.

Correctness depends on 0-based/1-based conventions, half-open intervals, sort order, strand, assembly, contig naming, and treatment of split reads; generic commands can silently produce plausible wrong overlaps.
CPM/RPKM/RPGC normalization and visualization depend on effective genome size, excluded regions, duplicates, depth, assay, and controls; heatmaps/correlation are not inferential validation.
Embeddings depend on genome build, token universe, training corpus, random seed, negative sampling, and model version; proximity in embedding space is not biological equivalence.
Fast interval/token operations remain sensitive to build, coordinate convention, universe construction and tokenizer version; performance claims are not locally benchmarked.
Peak calls depend on assay-specific shift/extsize, effective genome size, duplicates, controls, blacklist and replicate reproducibility; Poisson enrichment alone is not a validated regulatory site.
Duplicated BUSCOs count as complete by definition but may indicate haplotigs, contamination, polyploidy or assembly artifacts; lineage dataset name/version and expected biology must accompany scores.
Automatic adapter detection and generic quality trimming can remove biological sequence or bias short/low-complexity libraries; before/after QC and assay-specific parameters are required.
MultiQC aggregates tool logs but does not validate samples or define pass/fail; HTML can expose sample identifiers and paths, and parser results depend on tool/MultiQC versions.
Negative-binomial inference requires biological replication, correct design/contrast and confounder handling; a fixed count filter/LFC cutoff is not universal and tximeta may fetch mutable metadata.

Selecting strandedness by whichever mode assigns most reads is not a valid protocol check, and calling most polyA libraries unstranded is unsafe; annotation, multimappers, overlaps and paired-fragment semantics matter.
Remote Enrichr libraries change over time; ORA needs an explicit measured-gene universe and GSEA needs ranked statistics, identifier/species checks and multiple-testing-aware interpretation.
PyDESeq2 feature/version parity with DESeq2 is not established and examples assume adequate replication/design; shrinkage, contrasts, Cook filtering and fixed thresholds require validation.

Transcript-only and decoy-aware indexes are presented side-by-side without enforcing matching genome/annotation provenance; library type, bias options and gene summarization materially change results.

The broad API cookbook includes version-sensitive/deprecated alignment functions and no DOI citations; distance tests and ordinations require assumptions, permutations and sampling design not guaranteed by snippets.
Recipes mutate or overwrite H5AD/Zarr outputs and can densify huge matrices; raw-count, normalized, layer, gene-identity and backed-mode semantics need explicit invariants and privacy controls.

Pretrained labels are reference/model-version dependent and confidence is not calibrated for unseen tissues/disease states; downloaded pickle models and cell-level labels need provenance and manual validation.
Census schemas and stable/latest snapshots change; cross-study cells retain batch/protocol/consent limitations, and large local H5AD exports can contain donor/disease metadata.
The claim that Harmony removes batch while preserving biology is not guaranteed when batch and biology are confounded; overcorrection must be tested with held-out biology and uncorrected views.
Majority voting among correlated methods is not independent evidence or calibrated uncertainty; reference label quality, gene overlap and out-of-distribution cells govern validity.

The standard workflow uses fixed 200/5000/20% QC cutoffs, treats high gene count as doublets, regresses counts/mitochondrial fraction, and omits required dataset-specific doublet/ambient-RNA validation.
Deep models are stochastic and can overcorrect confounded biology; architecture/training/version/seed and count-layer assumptions must be pinned, and examples overwrite saved models.

The guide correctly warns about high-stakes claims but its three tiers are not independent evidence and cannot replace tissue-specific references, doublet/ambient-RNA QC, ontology mapping and expert adjudication.

Commands such as norm -d any delete duplicate records and filters can change cohort/genotype content; reference/build, left-normalization and provenance must be explicit before clinical or population use.
Copy-number calls depend on purity, ploidy, sex chromosomes, capture design, matched normals and segmentation; export to clinical formats does not make thresholds clinically validated.

A generic Best Practices sketch hard-codes old dbSNP/resource examples and calls GATK an NIH/ENCODE clinical standard without provenance; assay, pedigree, ploidy, contamination and validation remain unresolved.
GWAS requires phenotype/covariate QC, ancestry-aware structure, relatedness, imputation INFO, case/control-specific HWE decisions and privacy safeguards; generic thresholds are not universal.
HIGH predicted molecular consequence is not pathogenicity or clinical relevance; transcript/build/database choice, HGVS validation, inheritance and phenotype evidence are required.
QUAL is caller/model-specific evidence against the reference hypothesis, not a universal per-call error probability; blanket QUAL>=30 and fixed Ts/Tv targets can discard truth or retain artifacts.

Pin both client and data release and record collection/data-use constraints; installed-wheel index version controls results (210-212).; Do not assume public equals unrestricted; retain collection-level terms and avoid re-identification/linkage attempts.; Optional BigQuery crosses into credentials/billing and is outside auth-free claims (339-355).; Printing PatientID and shareable viewer URLs requires output-handling review even for public data (173-198).

Says nnU-Net automatically determines the optimal architecture and consistently achieves SOTA (11), which is not guaranteed for a new dataset.; A fixed 20-case threshold and production-pipeline recommendation (15-20,27) ignore task complexity, site shift, label quality and clinical validation.; The evaluation code names an average Hausdorff result hd95 and later reports 'Mean Avg HD', so metric semantics are inconsistent (348-403).; Example selects slices where prediction exists, which can hide false-negative slices and empty predictions in qualitative QC (425-431).; No patient-level/site-level split, leakage audit, external validation, uncertainty, calibration or clinical performance gate.

Useful candidate, but benchmark claims such as MiniROCKET ~75x and k=1 often best are context-specific. Dataset loaders imply network retrieval; evaluation examples need grouped/temporal split guidance where applicable.

Broad, generally sound candidate. Planck18 is called the current standard too categorically; cosmology must match study convention. FITS verify('fix') can silently mutate metadata and remote/SAMP capabilities need trust boundaries.

Valuable infrastructure knowledge, but distributed Dask transports serialized Python objects and exposes dashboards/schedulers; the guide lacks authentication/TLS/untrusted-worker warnings. Generic normalization code can cause leakage if applied before split.

The reporting idea is useful, but claims that zero variance makes t-tests and fold-change undefined are false in general, scipy ttest behavior is mischaracterized, and generic gene/event/batch thresholds can remove scientifically valid signals or induce selection bias. Filtering must be analysis-specific and prespecified.

Good intake checklist but too broad to be executable safely. It tells agents to install missing libraries and suggest normalization/imputation before experimental-design context is established. Vendor/clinical/genomic formats need dedicated validators.

CRS warnings are valuable. Basemap/database/remote-file examples need network and credential controls; area/distance accuracy needs explicit projection selection and geometry validity repair provenance.

High-risk automation: it repeatedly optimizes hypotheses against a validation set, which encourages adaptive overfitting and does not constitute scientific hypothesis testing. The quick start/API surface is unversioned; prompts may exfiltrate sensitive observations. No multiplicity, preregistration, independent replication or uncertainty contract.

Broad code cookbook. sudo apt install and direct MATLAB/Octave execution exceed safe skill behavior. MATLAB and Octave are not drop-in equivalent; examples require runtime-specific validation and toolbox license detection.

Pairwise n reporting is valuable, but it asserts bulk rank/corr is incorrect, uses arbitrary min_valid/50% thresholds, filters nunique<3 (excluding valid binary features), and omits multiple-testing correction and missingness-mechanism caveats. Pairwise deletion can yield non-positive-semidefinite correlation matrices and noncomparable n.

Reject. Installer downloads and extracts an unverified tarball and uses pip --break-system-packages. The purported mandatory third NEB gate becomes WARN and exit-success when trajectory is absent. Absence of a >2 kJ/mol interior well does not prove a single barrier. IRC plotting uses unaligned coordinate RMSD and selects the highest sampled frame as TS, so orientation/barrier can be wrong. No method uncertainty or electronic-structure adequacy gate can make xTB barriers quantitative.

Good general candidate. GraphML/GEXF are safer than pickle; any gpickle or arbitrary object-node serialization must be excluded. Algorithmic results depend on directedness, weights, disconnectedness, random seeds and resolution, which need stronger reporting.

Potentially valuable but biomedical signal pipelines need sampling-rate/device/artifact validation and cannot be treated as clinical interpretation. Default automated cleaning and HRV on short/noisy segments need modality-specific minimums and provenance.

Reject as operational recipe. It states questionable fixed channel counts/hardware requirements, duplicates the SpikeInterface skill, uses destructive remove_existing_folder=True, and relies on pre-0.101 extract_waveforms APIs while the sibling advertises SortingAnalyzer. QC thresholds are not ground-truth validation.

Workflow concepts are useful, but curl|bash remote-code execution, unpinned nf-core pipelines/containers, cloud/HPC executors and arbitrary process scripts are outside a safe general skill. Reproducibility requires immutable revision/container digests and explicit data egress policy.

Strong data-engineering candidate, but ancillary examples assign cloud secrets in process environment and include remote database/cloud writes without approval boundaries. Version-sensitive streaming/Excel/cloud APIs and performance claims need pins and fixtures.

Reject without clinical-data governance. It handles credentialed patient-level EHR but has no PHI/de-identification, DUA, secure storage, cohort leakage, temporal split, external validation, calibration, fairness, or clinical-use disclaimer. A patient split alone does not prevent temporal or site leakage.

Core local structure operations are promising. Credential examples encourage embedding a key in a Python command/SETTINGS and falling back to the literal your_key. Materials Project schemas and VASP defaults are version/pseudopotential sensitive; generated inputs are not scientifically validated calculations.

Useful candidate. Optimization output is stochastic and depends on scaling, constraint formulation, termination and seed; examples need repeated-run uncertainty and held-out objective evaluation where simulators/data-driven surrogates are involved.

Core pipeline guidance is reusable, but joblib.load is arbitrary code execution for untrusted files and is shown without warning. Generic random train/test and CV are unsafe for grouped, longitudinal, batch, repeated-measure or spatial scientific data; calibration and nested CV are not defaulted.

SHAP values explain a fitted model under a background/conditionality convention, not causality or feature truth. The skill needs correlated-feature, data-leakage and background-distribution guardrails. joblib.load of an explainer is unsafe for untrusted artifacts.

Strong conceptual candidate. Simulation conclusions require warm-up/burn-in, independent replications, uncertainty intervals, seed streams, verification/validation against real systems and sensitivity analysis; cookbook output alone is not evidence.

Reject as unrestricted skill: Snakemake rules execute arbitrary shell, remote downloads and cluster submissions. The example embeds wget in a rule and production submission commands. Dry-run validates the DAG, not shell safety, data provenance or scientific correctness.

Static reference has value, but containerized sorters and external binaries are arbitrary code execution. Sorter agreement is not ground truth; metric thresholds are probe/recording dependent. Rapid API change requires an exact SpikeInterface version and small public validation recording.

Good candidate. Generated C/Fortran and lambdified expressions need explicit symbol assumptions, domain/singularity checks, numerical verification and no automatic compilation/execution. Solver output can be conditional/incomplete.

Promising reference, but graph splits must prevent edge/node/scaffold/temporal leakage according to task. Dataset downloads and PyTorch checkpoints are external/untrusted artifacts. Accuracy examples lack repeated seeds and baselines.

Reject as-is. from_pretrained downloads mutable third-party code/weights; model licenses vary. Performance claims (5-15%, under an hour) lack matched benchmarks/hardware. Generated biomedical statements and naive drug-disease pair extraction can fabricate evidence; model output must never be treated as literature fact.

Contains overclaims that UMAP preserves global structure and that features must always be standardized. Scaling is metric/data dependent. Embeddings are exploratory and distances/clusters are parameter-sensitive; supervised UMAP must be fit inside CV, and clustering on a tuned embedding needs stability checks.

Reject because every REST example targets the legacy api.patentsview.org query surface and rate/auth claims are time-sensitive with no retrieval date. Patent keyword/assignee counts are not prior-art or freedom-to-operate conclusions; legal interpretation guardrails are absent.

Reject as-is. Billion-rows-per-second and 10-100x claims are hardware/workload dependent and unsourced. Python 3.7+ compatibility is stale/underspecified. Ancillary material demonstrates credentials in storage_options and an unauthenticated ws:// server pattern; persisted ML state is an untrusted artifact boundary.

Good candidate but highly version-sensitive across Zarr v2/v3 compressor/store/consolidation APIs. Cloud writes need credential/overwrite/consistency controls; chunk recommendations are heuristics and must be benchmarked on actual access patterns.

The PDF recipe explicitly imitates browser headers and warms a landing page to seek a Cloudflare trust cookie, an unreliable anti-bot workaround that should not be operationalized (404-432).; The skill hard-codes an 'as of 2026' access behavior without captured verification (404-406).

Claims a unique mandatory Ai/Aii hierarchy and strict display limits (99-114, 223-233) without dated evidence; must be checked against current article type and journal instructions.; Raster DPI metadata checks do not prove effective resolution at final placed size (21-49, 173-220).

Adopt only as generic workflow guidance; verify citations against primary records and current target-journal style rather than trusting examples.
